text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Public prosecutor accuses 71 companies of fraudulent use of European Union social funds totalling some seven billion escudos between 1987 and 1990.
- Justice Ministry drew up draft law weakening banking secrecy but Finance Minister Antonio de Sousa Franco opposes the project.
- Government approves 34.2 billion escudos of state financing for public companies, 10 billion escudos down on 1996. State airline TAP will get three billion.
- Police probe prostitution rings in investigation into Amarante fire which killed 12 people.
- Klaus Bunger, the president of the European Commission's Economic Policy Committee, sends letter to Finance Minister applauding the degree of "real" concvergence by Portuguese economy.
